what_was_found: The Stripe adapter's third checkout variant omitted payment_method_types, so an account that refused both card-only requests would have let Stripe choose the methods (Link, wallets, bank debits, asynchronous methods). PRE-LIVE never reached it, but nothing prevented it.
The hosted page offered Link ('Save my information for faster checkout') beside the card form even on a card-only session; Link may be reported as its own payment-method type.
Neither adapter checked, at capture, which method the client actually paid with.

A provider refund of the PRE-LIVE sandbox charge (recorded by the reconciler, settlement REVERSED) left the entitlement it paid for ACTIVE: a refund does not end access. Recorded as an open Product-Owner decision.
corrections_of_record: T0216 said the Managed Payments defect was 'fixed with card-only variants'. The fix as deployed in T0216 also carried a third variant that let Stripe choose the methods; it is removed here.
T0216 and current_delivery listed guest IPv6 forwarding, DNS tunnelling and the currency-conversion design as open decisions; all three were decided and implemented in T0216 itself.

Wait before another window (setting retry_after_minutes, default 30, 0-1440, audited with the others): a device may have another temporary-internet window once that long has passed since its last one ended; a window ended by choosing a different address does not start it; the daily limits still apply.

Staff help (migration 0113, contract 6.7): Sign-in methods -> Code requests lists the last 24 hours of code requests with the device, the code's state and the window. 'Let them try again' (code-requests write) marks the device's ended windows cleared so they stop counting; nothing is deleted and no access is granted. 'Show code' (code-reveal write) reads a live code from a sealed copy kept only while the code can be used. Both take the password and a reason and are audited without the code. Guest relations may clear but not reveal; a viewer reads the list.
